categories.question: You can illuminate one star model for a dark-sky display. Which light switches on?

outcomes.name: Red giant
outcomes.description: Red giant — large red-orange mottled glowing star

outcomes.name: White dwarf
outcomes.description: White dwarf — small brilliant white stellar orb

outcomes.name: Blue supergiant
outcomes.description: Blue supergiant — large vivid blue luminous star

outcomes.name: Pulsar
outcomes.description: Pulsar — dense purple star with two narrow beams and a glowing magnetic arc

categories.question: A planetarium artist asks you to choose a galaxy for the ceiling. Which shape do you draw?

outcomes.name: Barred spiral galaxy
outcomes.description: Barred spiral galaxy — galaxy with golden central bar and blue spiral arms

outcomes.name: Elliptical galaxy
outcomes.description: Elliptical galaxy — smooth amber oval glow of an elliptical galaxy

outcomes.name: Ring galaxy
outcomes.description: Ring galaxy — blue ring of stars around a bright separated core

outcomes.name: Irregular galaxy
outcomes.description: Irregular galaxy — asymmetric patchy star cloud without a clear disc

categories.question: A telescope image inspires your next postcard. Which cloud of gas do you frame?

outcomes.name: Horsehead Nebula
outcomes.description: Horsehead Nebula — dark horsehead silhouette against a small red emission cloud

outcomes.name: Ring Nebula
outcomes.description: Ring Nebula — glowing oval planetary nebula with blue centre

outcomes.name: Crab Nebula
outcomes.description: Crab Nebula — tangled orange and blue nebula filaments

outcomes.name: Butterfly Nebula
outcomes.description: Butterfly Nebula — bipolar nebula with two orange winglike lobes

categories.question: You can stay up late for one sky event. Which one goes on your calendar?

outcomes.name: Solar eclipse
outcomes.description: Solar eclipse — black lunar disc with a white solar corona

outcomes.name: Meteor shower
outcomes.description: Meteor shower — cluster of parallel bright meteor streaks

outcomes.name: Planetary conjunction
outcomes.description: Planetary conjunction — two differently sized luminous planets appearing close together
